newsitem.title: USA: CIA investigator said to extend probe on crack sales.
newsitem.headline: CIA investigator said to extend probe on crack sales.

text.p: The CIA's internal watchdog has decided to extend an investigation into reports that the spy agency was involved in drug trafficking in the 1980s to support rebels fighting Nicaragua's Sandinista government, the Washington Post reported in Saturday editions.
CIA Inspector General Frederick Hitz "is working as fast as he can, but he doesn't want to be tied to a date," the newspaper quoted a CIA spokesman as saying.
Hitz has decided he needs much more than the planned two months to do a "thorough and complete" investigation, the spokesman said.
The internal probe by the Central Intelligence Agency and a separate investigation by the Justice Department were triggered by a series of reports in the San Jose Mercury News.
The reports said the Nicaraguan Contra rebels played a leading role in introducing crack cocaine into U.S. ghettoes in the 1980s to raise money to fight the leftist government.
Last month, CIA Director John Deutch said Hitz's review would be completed within 60 days.

The Post quoted present and former CIA officers saying that one reason for the delay was the vast number of reports on drug trafficking from CIA officers in the Central American region that must be reviewed.
